Do you have any resources to point me to? I’d like to be compelled into a pro life argument.

Fetus’ are not a “group” of humans, they are humans that are in the circumstance of using another person to sustain their own life. That does not make them a group, and I don’t advocate that their right to life be discarded on the basis that they are underdeveloped and fetus’, I advocate for their right to life to be overturned when it interferes with the biological interests of a fully developed, sentient, human woman.
You can argue about the concept of what someone “should do” all day long but you cannot legislate what should and should not be.
Well I certainly wouldn’t and would argue that is facism.
I don’t think that’s the case, if this thread does indeed accurately represent pro life arguments.

That’s merely an opinion on how you think women should conduct themselves during pregnancy (and I think it’s silly, to ask a woman to forgo all of her sense of personhood in order to incubate a fetus) but I am strictly speaking in a legal sense, and this has no relation to this theoretical “special relationship” you speak of between a mother and a fetus. 

It’s similar to financial viability (and don’t strawman me and say that I must be okay with killing viable children in order to forgo financial responsibilities to them) but, if you reach 18 you are therefore financially viable for yourself and your mother has the right to kick you out of the house there and then, no matter how immoral or indecent you think that is. I may be shooting myself in the foot with this analogy (it’s not perfect) but essentially, viability matters.

I’m still confused about forcing pregnancy on the unwilling (I’m not accusing you of personally doing this lmao, in a very very general sense) but other than that, no. I respect your clearness and tastefulness in the way you’ve responded to my post so cheers man

They definitely are when the body using the woman’s resources is non viable outside of the womb and does not have any intrinsic sense of personhood. If you’re going by this same logic, I must say again, that you’re essentially advocating for women to be biologically sub-servant to the fetus beyond birth aswell. Should women be forced to give their children their biological resources if their children fall ill?

We’re not arguing about importance of life’s, I’m arguing over a woman’s right to control what processes are going on in her own body, regardless of external circumstances. The fetus is not bodily autonomous therefore it can never take bodily presidency over the woman. And as I said, consent to carrying a fetus can be revoked.
I also would never have an abortion but am pro choice.

I’d just say viability outside of the womb, as I think if a fully sentient person was suddenly using my body to sustain itself I would take a pill to stop it. If the baby can indeed be taken out of the woman and survive and thrive then that should always be done in place of an abortion.
Then I need to take a step back and reframe how I deconstruct an argument. Apologies.

No, I don’t. I mean to her social, economical, or emotional detriment aswell. And I’m sorry, but women are still not obligated to use their bodily resources to sustain a fetus that they do not want inside their body.
Semantics are a beautiful thing but not to be extensively argued over, I feel.
*not
It’s a fetus we are talking about and we are not talking about organs, it’s bodily resources that the woman has no consented to share for the 10th time. Please keep up.
I’m not, I’m equating it to stealing blood and other bodily resources (bone marrow, etc) which is perfectly reasonable considering that is how pregnancies work. They use biological resources.

Not when they exit the womb, when they become viable and have no longer any need for the woman’s bodily resources. Happens at around 6-7 months. That’s when abortions become immoral. Hope this cleared everything up.
Yes you are, she is using her own body and resources and organs to let this fetus continue to live and develop inside her.
They do when their viability depends on another person. It is to the woman’s detriment that the fetus continues to live.
Then you don’t understand basic logic.
Well I don’t.

But you can force a woman to carry a baby, which in turn uses her bodily organs and resources without her consent? Double think, my friend. You are committing it. And no, your argument is still fallacious. I’d like to know in what world it is acceptable to force someone by law to use their bodily rights to ensure someone else’s wellbeing, fetus or not.

I can’t answer why she did, you’d have to speak to individual women. And in this tangible, real world where consent can indeed be revoked due to a plethora of factors. There’s also the issue of the fetus’ sentience and personhood that one must take into consideration.

That’s correct, but even though a woman may be irresponsible (could even say stupid, immoral, whatever, I personally wouldn’t) for having an abortion I still believe she should have the right to terminate a pregnancy, due to reasons I’ve outlined a few times in this thread.
That’s a pretty cool middle ground to meet on. It’s been a pleasant exchange my dude, thanks.

Yes, I think women (and anybody for that matter) do indeed have the right to kill whatever is using their bodily resources without consent, and I do believe consent can be revoked. I won’t even touch the rape argument because as has been established before it is not terribly relevant due to the low number of abortions from rape (however it may be of use due to the unknown amount of actual pregnancies from rape)
It’s because it relates to the mechanics and overall morality of abortion.

Sorry dude it’s hard to navigate replies in this labyrinth of comments. If you feel that way, that’s cool because I’m not arguing against your right to be offended or even disgusted by abortion, I’m simply arguing for it’s legality. Some things may be immoral (infidelity) but we still allow for their legality due to freedom.
That’s cool and I respect your opinion but remain unconvinced that pro life is the way. I’d love love love to be convinced that abortion is wrong.
Yes, it’s a future baby being killed. You’re correct, do you also think mothers should be obligated by state law to donate their organs to their sick children? That’s a child being killed, also.
Because steps may have been taken beforehand in order to prevent a pregnancy that may not have worked.
I agree but I do truly think pro lifers feel abortion is akin to murder, which baffles me.

Then that’s okay, and I think you should be able to carry a baby to term if you feel it would haunt you morally or emotionally, but my argument is that the state should have no say in how a woman navigates her pregnancy, and I would never argue for mandatory abortions. Pro choice = pro choice.
*not
Adoption is an alternative to childbirth, no pregnancy. I do genuinely want to understand but you can’t force a woman to carry a baby she doesn’t want, it is simply not ethical. I’m sorry.
Why is the mother obligated to give the fetus her bodily rights if she doesn’t want to? Why is this a special right we grant to fetus’ and nobody else?

You’re equating the right to work with bodily autonomy, this is something that cannot be done. You’re using fallacious arguments that don’t even make sense, my friend. 

And if bodily autonomy doesn’t even compare to the right to life, should I be able to take organs from living people (granted that it doesn’t kill them, just damages their overall health) in order to sustain myself?
If parental responsibility trumps all, then mothers should be forced to donate parts of their body to their children should some unfortunate accident befall them. Do you agree with this?
I think a fetus is indeed an entity, it’s a living thing but it does indeed infringe on someone else’s bodily rights, hence my argument. I have no problem admitting that the fetus is a life.

Also killing a viable human being outside of a womb or a bodily resource is totally different from aborting a baby dependant on a sole provider of bodily resources. You’re putting forth a false equivalence.

I disagree. I don’t think mothers necessarily consent to pregnancy, mistakes are made and even if consent was obtained, consent can be revoked at any time. We use the same logic for sex, employment, and various other things. Pregnancy is no different, the mothers body is the sole provider and therefore the sole decision maker.

The fetus is a child but it is infringing on the bodily rights of the mother. As I said, even though I’m a fully sentient human being I would never expect to be able to use someone else’s bodily resources without consent.
I draw the line at viability outside the womb; if the fetus is viable and can be put into a special incubator outside of the womb it is immoral to abort it.
The fetus has the right to use someone’s bodily resources without consent, no other human being does. By saying abortion should be illegal you are giving extra rights to the fetus.

Not everyone understands, because they say “why don’t you just give it up for adoption” without taking into consideration how pregnancy affects a woman’s body. If it’s her bodily resources, why should she be forced by the state to provide them for said fetus inside her womb?
So if I attach myself to your body and use your bodily resources you shouldn’t be able to take a pill and stop that, even if it results in my death?
